# Exact pointed critical-section identities for one actual H group

This note records a finite-menu identity useful when seeking a weaker cap-comparison object than a pointwise density minorant. It supplies no sharp mass inequality by itself.

Assume the full-rank one-group geometry and SAME actual separator of `candidate 8effe5eb4947ba88`. Write the common outer envelope as K_z subset y(z)+ell(z)D, with affine y and positive affine ell. Sources Y_a=(p_a,y(p_a)) satisfy f_H(Y_a)=ell(p_a) f_D. Let kappa_a be the actual contact coefficients, K=sum_a kappa_a>0, and

    pbar=sum_a kappa_a p_a/K,
    ellbar=ell(pbar),
    deltabar=sum_a kappa_a delta_a/K
             =epsilon f_D ellbar.

For cap j let sigma_j be its actual effective physical section measure, including the selected outside-support density from the single separator. Its total mass is T_j>0 and its first moment is m_j. The proper sections use H_(d-1)/|u_j|; a supporting section uses that same coarea normalization times its retained selector. No inside-support section is inserted.

The signed full cap-normal equations give

    m_j/T_j=(pbar,y(pbar))
                    -epsilon f_D ellbar (0,grad Gamma(u_j)),   (1)
    omega_j T_j=rho_j K.                                       (2)

These equations follow directly by setting each full normal velocity to both signs in the branch-dual functional: its coefficient is rho_j sum_a kappa_a Y_a minus rho_j sum_a kappa_a delta_a (0,grad Gamma) minus omega_j m_j. Equation (2) is the already retained coarea normalization. All source multiplicities remain present in kappa_a.

Define the POINTED selected section measure by pushing ell(z) sigma_j under

    (z,x) -> xi=(x-y(z))/ell(z).

Call it tilde sigma_j and its mass tilde T_j. Since ell is affine, the base component of (1) gives

    tilde T_j=integral ell(z) d sigma_j=ellbar T_j.              (3)

Since y is affine, the continuous component of (1) gives

    integral xi d tilde sigma_j
      =integral [x-y(z)] d sigma_j
      =-epsilon f_D ellbar T_j grad Gamma(u_j).                 (4)

Consequently

    barycenter(tilde sigma_j)=-epsilon f_D grad Gamma(u_j),
    omega_j tilde T_j=ellbar rho_j K.                           (5)

This is an exact finite-epsilon statement. The pointed cap plane is u_j·xi=-epsilon f_D Gamma(u_j); Euler's identity u_j·grad Gamma=Gamma verifies that the barycenter in (5) lies in that plane.

On a proper slice in fiber z, sigma_j transforms with factor ell(z)^(d-1). Multiplication by ell(z) therefore gives ell(z)^d H_(d-1)/|u_j|, exactly the section weight of the actual pointed density

    f(xi)=sum_z ell(z)^d 1_(D_z)(xi).

The same selector is retained on a supporting facet. Thus (5) describes actual generalized sections of f, not a new marginal or an arbitrary trace choice. In particular every selected section has pointed centroid zero at epsilon=0, while its finite-buffer displacement is the common covariance-norm gradient above.

These identities can also be understood as the normal-stationarity conditions for the selected pointed cap functional. They do not turn f into a log-concave or inverse-power-concave density. Nor do section-centroid equalities alone imply a Gamma_d depth theorem for arbitrary densities. Any finite-menu polar construction using (5) still has to use cross-base compatibility and the actual common-Q/deepestness constraints to derive a sharp mass comparison.
